pull.title: test: fix coinbases built on arbitrary parents
pull.body:
**Problem:** Test helpers that attach active-tip templates to arbitrary parents retain the template's subsidy.
Existing reorg tests can underpay without failing, while a fork crossing a halving can overpay and fail with `bad-cb-amount`.
Bare height scripts at heights 1 through 16 also fail with `bad-cb-length`.

**Fix:** Share parent-dependent reconstruction between `BuildChain()` and `MinerTestingSetup::Block()`, deriving difficulty and coinbase fields from the actual parent.
Pad rebuilt coinbase input scripts and require coinbase-only templates so recalculating the subsidy cannot discard transaction fees.

Built each commit and ran the unit tests, with a before and after of both cases against master.

Rebased to resolve conflicts and applied the review suggestions.
The block’s difficulty now uses its actual parent and timestamp, and its coinbase pays the subsidy for its resulting height.
I also added focused tests for the target and coinbase fields through the first halving.

comments.body:
This is an assignment rather than an adjustment, so the template's fees go with it. `MinerTestingSetup::Block` asks for its template with the mempool on, and with one transaction in it the coinbase reward comes out at 5000001000 on master and 5000000000 here, with the block still carrying that transaction.

Nothing hits it today, since the mempool is empty at every call. Would `.use_mempool = false` on that template call be simpler? It makes the site match `BuildChain`, so the overwrite is exact, and the three suites stay green with it.
Sure, added `.use_mempool = false` to `MinerTestingSetup::Block()` and asserted the shared helper receives a coinbase-only block.
Thanks! I added similar tests, with the coinbase cases combined into one fork test. I also credited you as a co-author on the commits containing them.
